parameters.name: Customer definition — residential scope
parameters.doc_value: persons who have agreed to pay for electric service exclusively for residential purposes
parameters.s1_quote: for the purposes of sections 13(d), 15, and 16 of this rule, the term shall be limited to mean persons who have agreed to pay for such service exclusively for residential purposes

parameters.name: Delinquency period
parameters.doc_value: seventeen (17) days after the initial bill is postmarked
parameters.s1_quote: a bill is considered delinquent unless payment is received within seventeen (17) days after the initial bill is postmarked

parameters.name: Late payment charge — first $3
parameters.doc_value: ten percent (10%) of the first three dollars ($3)
parameters.s1_quote: the late payment charge shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the first three dollars ($3) and three percent (3%) of the excess of three dollars ($3)

parameters.name: Late payment charge — excess over $3
parameters.doc_value: three percent (3%) of the excess of three dollars ($3)
parameters.s1_quote: the late payment charge shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the first three dollars ($3) and three percent (3%) of the excess of three dollars ($3)

parameters.name: Residential disconnect notice period
parameters.doc_value: fourteen (14) days prior written notice
parameters.s1_quote: electric service to any residential customer shall not be disconnected for a violation of any rule or regulation of a utility or for the nonpayment of a bill, except after fourteen (14) days prior written notice to the customer

parameters.name: Medical certificate postponement — first
parameters.doc_value: ten (10) days
parameters.s1_quote: a utility shall postpone the disconnection of service for ten (10) days if, prior to the disconnect date specified in the disconnect notice, the customer provides the utility with a medical statement

parameters.name: Medical certificate postponement — renewal
parameters.doc_value: one (1) additional ten (10) day period
parameters.s1_quote: the postponement of disconnection shall be continued for one (1) additional ten (10) day period upon the provision of an additional such medical statement

parameters.name: Winter protection period start
parameters.doc_value: December 1
parameters.s1_quote: during the period from december 1 through march 15, disconnect electric residential service to any customer who either is receiving or who is eligible for and has applied for assistance under ic 4-4-33

parameters.name: Winter protection period end
parameters.doc_value: March 15
parameters.s1_quote: during the period from december 1 through march 15, disconnect electric residential service to any customer who either is receiving or who is eligible for and has applied for assistance under ic 4-4-33

parameters.name: Application-pending protection trigger
parameters.doc_value: eligibility being determined by IHCDA or designee after submission of complete application
parameters.s1_quote: the customers' eligibility to receive benefits pursuant to ic 4-4-33 is being determined by the indiana housing and community development authority or its designee after the submission of a complete application for benefits by the customer

parameters.name: Payment arrangement down payment — dollar cap
parameters.doc_value: not to exceed ten dollars ($10) or one-tenth (1/10) of the bill, whichever is less
parameters.s1_quote: pays a reasonable portion (not to exceed ten dollars ($10) or one-tenth (1/10) of the bill, whichever is less, unless the customer agrees to a greater portion) of the bill

parameters.name: Payment arrangement term — financial hardship
parameters.doc_value: three (3) months
parameters.s1_quote: agrees to pay the remainder of the outstanding bill within three (3) months

parameters.name: Payment arrangement breach lookback
parameters.doc_value: twelve (12) months
parameters.s1_quote: has not breached any similar agreement with the utility made pursuant to this section within the past twelve (12) months

parameters.name: Utility-error arrangement down payment
parameters.doc_value: not to exceed an amount equal to the customer's average bill for the six (6) bills immediately preceding the bill in question
parameters.s1_quote: pays a reasonable portion of the bill, not to exceed an amount equal to the customer's average bill for the six (6) bills immediately preceding the bill in question

parameters.name: Deposit cap — fraction of annual billings
parameters.doc_value: one-sixth (1/6) of the expected annual billings
parameters.s1_quote: the amount of such deposit may not exceed an amount equal to one-sixth ( 1 /6) of the expected annual billings for the customer at the address at which service is rendered

parameters.name: Deposit installment threshold
parameters.doc_value: seventy dollars ($70)
parameters.s1_quote: the utility shall provide the customer with two (2) monthly billing cycles (approximately sixty (60) days) in which to pay any deposit that exceeds seventy dollars ($70)

parameters.name: Deposit payment period for deposits > $70
parameters.doc_value: two (2) monthly billing cycles (approximately sixty (60) days)
parameters.s1_quote: the utility shall provide the customer with two (2) monthly billing cycles (approximately sixty (60) days) in which to pay any deposit that exceeds seventy dollars ($70)

parameters.name: Permitted disconnection hours — start
parameters.s1_quote: no utility may disconnect service unless it is done between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., prevailing local time

parameters.name: Permitted disconnection hours — end
parameters.s1_quote: no utility may disconnect service unless it is done between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m., prevailing local time

parameters.name: Field contact record retention minimum
parameters.doc_value: at least thirty (30) days
parameters.s1_quote: make a record thereof to be maintained for at least thirty (30) days

parameters.name: Reconnection timing — regulatory minimum
parameters.doc_value: within one (1) working day
parameters.s1_quote: the utility must reconnect the service to the customer or user as soon as reasonably possible but at least within one (1) working day after it is requested to do so if the customer has satisfied the requirements of this rule

parameters.name: Customer window to file IURC informal complaint
parameters.doc_value: within seven (7) days of receiving RPL's proposed resolution
parameters.s1_quote: advise the customer that if he or she is not satisfied with the utility's proposed resolution, the customer may submit an informal complaint to consumer affairs within seven (7) days of the date the proposed resolution is received

parameters.name: Post-decision disconnection hold
parameters.doc_value: not sooner than ten (10) days after a decision by consumer affairs or the commission
parameters.s1_quote: sooner than ten (10) days after a decision by consumer affairs or the commission

parameters.name: Undisputed payment amount — fraction of annual billing
parameters.doc_value: one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual billing
parameters.s1_quote: if a customer and utility cannot agree what portion of the charges in a bill is undisputed, to avoid disconnection, the customer should pay on the disputed bill an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual billing for service to be rendered to the customer

parameters.name: Billing history for undisputed estimate (12+ month customers)
parameters.doc_value: twelve (12) months immediately preceding the disputed bill
parameters.s1_quote: for a customer who has been a customer for at least twelve (12) months, the estimate will be based on the customer's average bill for the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the disputed bill

parameters.name: Dispute records retention
parameters.doc_value: six (6) months from the date of final resolution
parameters.s1_quote: the utility shall retain records of disputes received under this rule and the resolutions thereof for a period of six (6) months from the date of final resolution of the dispute under this rule

coverage.reason: Billing adjustment rules are the primary subject of RPL-CS-PRO-007 (T15). This procedure references billing error as a disconnection-deferral condition at clause 11.3 (170 IAC 4-1-16(c)(3)), which is the relevant operational intersection.

interpretations.question: 170 IAC 4-1-16.5 defines 'disconnect' for EAP purposes — does it apply to RPL's main disconnection rule?
interpretations.position: 170 IAC 4-1-16.5 provides definitions specifically for the home energy assistance context (170 IAC 4-1). RPL applies those definitions consistently throughout its EAP and winter protection procedures, as they are more specific for that context.
interpretations.rationale: More protective reading applies EAP definitions broadly.

interpretations.question: The pack does not define 'business day' or 'company holidays' for disconnection purposes. What constitutes a business day for RPL?
interpretations.position: RPL defines business day as Monday through Friday excluding RPL Company holidays, which are the nine days listed in Section 3.15. This is consistent with 170 IAC 16-1-3(b) time computation rules and represents company practice.
interpretations.rationale: Company practice aligned to IAC time computation rule.

interpretations.question: 170 IAC 4-1-16(c) does not specify whether medical notice may be oral. How does RPL handle oral medical claims?
interpretations.position: RPL accepts oral medical claims as triggering an immediate suspension of disconnection, followed by a written certificate requirement. This is the most protective reading of the regulation.
interpretations.rationale: More protective reading; aligns with utility industry practice for customer-facing rules.

notes: 170 IAC 4-1-16.5 provides definitions for the EAP context only and is covered implicitly through the use of EAP-specific terms in clauses 3.11, 10.2, and 10.3. 170 IAC 4-1-16.6 is in the pack with full text including December 1 through March 15 dates and was cited directly per the pre-flight note.
